findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_address, check_endpoint, submit_feedback · Private data: check_xrpl_token, check_address, check_endpoint, token_holders, resolve_asset, verify_price, quote_amm, find_best_path, watch_token · Public sink: check_address, token_holders, submit_feedback · Destructive: check_transaction.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_address, check_endpoint, submit_feedback · Private data: check_xrpl_token, check_address, check_endpoint, token_holders, resolve_asset, verify_price, quote_amm, find_best_path, watch_token · Public sink: check_address, token_holders, submit_feedback · Destructive: check_transaction

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_xrpl_token" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
